passage:
Chinmay heard it through the bedroom wall: his parents arguing in low voices about fees and a loan. His stomach dropped, and then a guilty thought came, that his tuition was the reason. Next morning he asked his mother, "Is money really tight? Can I do something?" She told him a little and said the rest was for grown-ups to sort out. He decided to sell his old comics at school, and stopped there.

At lunch Ganga showed off her new phone and a photo from a trip to the hills. Chinmay smiled and said nothing, feeling bitter enough to notice it. Later he thought, I have my cricket team and my own room, and I am not going to borrow money just to pretend.

That night an ad flashed on his screen: "Turn ten rupees into a thousand with our betting app." His thumb hovered. Then he closed it and told his mother.

On Sunday Vinita, a relative, came for tea and mentioned with a pleasant smile that the term fees had been paid "just as we agreed". Chinmay's face went hot; he was thankful and ashamed in the same breath. He said, "Thank you, truly. I will pay it back one day," and meant it. Afterwards he asked his parents quietly whether they could gently ask Vinita to leave the fees out of tea-table talk. His father nodded slowly and said he would.

qa.q: What did Chinmay decide to sell at school?
qa.a: He decided to sell his old comics.

qa.q: How did Chinmay's reaction to the betting ad differ from his reaction to Vinita's remark about the fees?
qa.a: He closed the betting ad and told his mother, because the ad was a stranger's offer of quick money. Vinita, a relative, was helping with the fees, so Chinmay felt thankful and ashamed together and asked his parents to gently set a boundary.

qa.q: What was Chinmay feeling when Ganga showed her new phone?
qa.a: He felt bitter, and he noticed it instead of hiding it or acting on it.

qa.q: What could Chinmay do next if he starts to feel guilty about the family's money worries again?
qa.a: He could ask his parents what is happening, offer help that fits a child's role like selling comics, and remember he is not the one who has to fix the debts.

grounding: One family's money trouble is seen through a teen's worry and guilt, an online get-rich ad, envy of a friend and a relative's help that brings both thanks and shame.
